page: Amazon Web Services c7a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1994.0 and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 13.79 GB/sec. Text processing also ranks in the top 25% with a score of 2762.0. Multi-core performance is average, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 10286.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 18308.68. Large-block uncached read memory bandwidth is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% at 38.63 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads reach 1185.57 GB/sec.

The c7a.2xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that require high-frequency dedicated cores but do not demand massive memory footprints or local storage. It is well-suited for tasks such as single-threaded data processing, software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight LLM text generation using small models. However, it is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM inference due to its 16.0 GB memory limit and lower uncached memory bandwidth.
